findings.title: Blocked-email lookups are case-sensitive
findings.body: The lookup uses the submitted email verbatim, while email addresses are treated case-insensitively elsewhere in the application (for example, `change_email` lowercases them). A blocked address stored as `user@example.com` can therefore be used to register as `User@Example.com`, bypassing the block. Normalize the lookup and stored addresses consistently before comparing.

findings.title: Concurrent matches lose statistics increments
findings.body: This read-modify-save sequence is not atomic: simultaneous matches can both read the same `match_count` and save the same increment, losing one or more matches. Since the method is called during validation on signup, match statistics become unreliable under concurrent requests. Use an atomic database increment and update the timestamp.

findings.title: Rejected-email list is shared between controller instances
findings.body: `rejectedEmails` is a mutable array defined on the controller extension object, so controller instances can share it rather than each getting a fresh list. After one signup attempt rejects an address, a later account-creation modal can incorrectly mark that address invalid without contacting the server. Initialize the array per controller instance.
